issues.summary: Add PayNow QR as a checkout option for SME businesses
issues.description:
Background:
SME businesses on our hosted checkout keep asking for PayNow. A large share of their buyers in Singapore do not use credit cards for purchases under SGD 200 and abandon the cart when card entry is the only option.

Goal:
Let buyers pay from any Singapore banking app by scanning a PayNow QR. Funds land in the existing SGD collection account, so Finance sees PayNow takings next to card takings.

Scope:
- Generate a dynamic PayNow QR (SGQR format) for every SGD order on the hosted checkout page
- Expire each QR in 10 minutes and generate a fresh one on the same page
- Confirm the order by webhook from the collection bank, with polling as a fallback
- Keep card checkout exactly as it is; PayNow only appears for SGD orders
- Ship behind the paynow-checkout flag so it can be rolled out gradually

Acceptance criteria:
- The buyer sees the QR within 2 seconds of choosing PayNow
- Order confirmation within 30 seconds of the bank transfer in 99% of cases
- An expired QR cannot be paid; the bank returns those funds automatically
- The ops dashboard shows PayNow volume and confirmation latency per business

Out of scope: PayNow refunds (tracked separately) and non-SGD currencies.
Requested by Priya Nair (Product).

comments.author: ShiHan
comments.text: QR generation and the bank webhook handler are behind the paynow-checkout flag. End-to-end tests in staging pass for SGD 1.00, SGD 199.99 and SGD 5,000.00 orders, and the sandbox bank refuses an expired QR as expected.

comments.author: Zhao
comments.text: Good to go for a gradual rollout. Turn it on for 10% of SME businesses first and watch confirmation latency for a full week before going wider. If p99 latency goes above 30 seconds, switch back to card-only.

comments.author: ShiHan
comments.text: Week one at 10%: 4,812 PayNow orders, p99 confirmation latency 7.6 seconds, no stuck orders. Moved to 50% on Monday.

comments.author: ShiHan
comments.text: Four days at 50% with the same latency profile. Released to all SME businesses; the paynow-checkout flag stays in place as a kill switch until the end of the month.

issues.summary: FX amounts off by 0.01 on multi-currency invoices
issues.description:
Summary:
Invoices issued in USD and converted to SGD can disagree with the books by SGD 0.01. The invoicing module rounds every line item to two decimals before adding the lines up, while the accounting system converts the unrounded total once.

Steps to reproduce:
- Issue a USD invoice with three line items of USD 33.33 each
- Convert it to SGD at the daily rate (1.3127 on 2026-10-08)
- Compare the invoice total (SGD 131.25) with the journal entry (SGD 131.26)

Expected:
A single rounding step, at the invoice total, so the invoice and the journal entry always agree.

Scope:
- Fix the rounding order in the invoicing module
- Backfill the invoices issued since 1 October that carry a 0.01 difference
- Add regression tests with three-line and seven-line invoices

Spotted by Finance (Sheldon) in the September close.

comments.author: ShiHan
comments.text: Reproduced with the three-line USD invoice above: SGD 131.25 on the invoice, SGD 131.26 in the journal. The fix rounds once at the invoice total; the PR is up with the regression tests.

comments.author: Zhao
comments.text: Please backfill the 14 invoices issued since 1 October before closing this, and send Sheldon the list so Finance can adjust the September close if needed.

comments.author: ShiHan
comments.text: Backfill script dry-run in staging: 14 invoices, each off by exactly SGD 0.01, nine in our favour and five against. I will run it once the PR merges and send Sheldon the list.

issues.summary: Add a circuit breaker to the card-network client
issues.description:
Background:
Action item from INC-CARD-014 on 2026-08-12. The card network answered slowly for 38 minutes. Our checkout waited up to 30 seconds on each call, request handlers piled up, and card checkout degraded for every business.

Plan:
- Wrap the card-network client in a circuit breaker
- Trip the breaker at 20 consecutive responses slower than 3 seconds
- While the breaker is tripped, return a retryable error so the checkout page offers PayNow instead of hanging
- Let one probe call through every 30 seconds and close the breaker on 5 healthy responses in a row
- Show the breaker state on the checkout dashboard and page on-call when it trips

Acceptance criteria:
- A replay of the 2026-08-12 traffic in staging keeps checkout responsive (p99 under 2 seconds)
- The breaker state appears on the dashboard within 10 seconds

Requested by Dev Kumar (Platform).

comments.author: ShiHan
comments.text: The breaker is in place behind a config switch. The 2026-08-12 replay in staging held p99 at 1.4 seconds; without the breaker it climbed to 29 seconds.

comments.author: Zhao
comments.text: Ship it. Make sure the page to on-call names the card network that tripped, not just that something tripped.

comments.author: ShiHan
comments.text: Deployed to production with the network name in the page. In the 2026-09-02 card-network slowdown it tripped twice, checkout fell back to PayNow as planned, and nobody had to step in.

issues.summary: Run a standby-region switchover drill for the card-network gateway
issues.description:
Background:
Action item from INC-CARD-014. We have never moved card-network gateway traffic to the standby region outside a test plan, so we do not know how long it takes or what breaks along the way.

Plan:
- Switch staging gateway traffic to the standby region using the regional DNS weights
- Measure how long the switch takes end to end and count retried card authorisations
- Switch back and confirm the primary region takes the full load again
- Record durations, surprises and the exact commands in the card-network playbook

Exit criteria:
- The switch completes in under 5 minutes
- No card authorisation is lost; retries are acceptable

Requested by Maya Tan (SRE).

comments.author: ShiHan
comments.text: Staging drill complete. The switch took 4 min 10 s end to end; 37 card authorisations were retried and none were lost. The DNS weights took 2 min 40 s to take effect, which is most of the delay.

comments.author: Zhao
comments.text: Good result. Book the production drill for the November maintenance window, and add a step to lower the DNS TTL a day in advance.

comments.author: ShiHan
comments.text: Production drill booked for 2026-11-14, 02:00 SGT. The TTL step is in the card-network playbook.

issues.summary: Quarterly rotation of card-gateway API keys
issues.description:

Checklist:

Notes:

- Next rotation due: 2026-12-30

comments.author: Ivan

comments.author: Zhao

issues.summary: Increase the batch queue-depth alert threshold
issues.description:
Problem:
The batch queue-depth alert pages on-call at 5,000 queued jobs. It fires repeatedly in every month-end run, clears on its own within minutes, and has paged on-call on 23 occasions in the past 30 days with no visible effect. On-call now ignores it, which is worse than having no alert at all.

Plan:
- Lift the threshold to 20,000 queued jobs
- Add a second rule that pages when a job waits longer than 15 minutes, which is the real warning sign
- Keep a non-paging dashboard tile at 5,000 for visibility

Evidence:
The September month-end run peaked at 14,200 queued jobs and drained in 11 minutes without a single late job.

Requested by Wei Ling (SRE).

comments.author: ShiHan
comments.text: Agree with the plan. The September month-end run peaked at 14,200 queued jobs and drained in 11 minutes, so 20,000 leaves headroom.

comments.author: Zhao
comments.text: Fine by me, but ship the 15-minute wait rule in the same release so we keep the coverage.

issues.summary: Instant payouts to IDR bank accounts (Q4 roadmap)

issues.summary: Payout CSV uses UTC instead of SGT for the daily cut-off
issues.description:
Summary:
The daily payout CSV labels its cut-off as 23:59 SGT but applies it in UTC. Transfers between 08:00 and 23:59 SGT land in the next day's file, so the CSV totals disagree with the bank statement for that day.

Steps to reproduce:
- Send a payout at 09:00 SGT
- Download the payout CSV for that date
- The payout is missing and appears in the next day's file instead

Expected:
The cut-off is applied in the Asia/Singapore zone, as labelled.

Scope:
- Convert the cut-off to Asia/Singapore before filtering
- Add tests at the 07:59, 08:00 and 23:59 SGT boundaries
- Regenerate the files for the past 30 days and notify the businesses whose files moved

Requested by Wei Ling (SRE).

comments.author: ShiHan
comments.text: Confirmed: the filter compares UTC timestamps against a 23:59 SGT label. The fix converts the cut-off to Asia/Singapore before filtering; tests for the 07:59, 08:00 and 23:59 boundaries are in the PR.

comments.author: Zhao
comments.text: Before regenerating old files, check with Sheldon whether Finance has already booked against the old files.

comments.author: ShiHan
comments.text: Sheldon confirmed Finance books from the bank statement, not the CSV, so regenerating the past 30 days is safe. Regeneration runs once the fix ships.

issues.summary: Remove the deprecated v1 refunds endpoint
issues.description:
Background:
/v1/refunds was replaced by /v2/refunds in March. No client has called /v1/refunds since 2026-07-01, based on 90 days of API gateway logs, and the endpoint carries its own copy of the refund rules, which keeps drifting from v2.

Plan:
- Return 410 Gone with a pointer to /v2/refunds for one release
- Delete the handler, its tests and the duplicated refund rules
- Remove the endpoint from the public API reference and the SDKs

Risk:
Low. If an unknown client appears, the 410 response tells it exactly where to go.

Requested by Dev Kumar (Platform).

comments.author: ShiHan
comments.text: Checked again: zero calls to /v1/refunds in the gateway logs for the past 90 days, including the month-end peaks.

comments.author: Zhao
comments.text: Go ahead for the next release. Send the 410 notice to the developer mailing list a week before.

issues.summary: Patch TLS settings flagged by the PCI DSS scan
issues.description:
Problem:
The external PCI DSS vulnerability scan flagged TLS 1.0 enabled on two card-data hosts, cde-web-01 and cde-web-02. PCI DSS requires TLS 1.2 or higher on every host in the cardholder data environment, so this blocks a passing scan.

Plan:
- Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1 on both hosts and limit ciphers to the allowed list
- Re-run the external scan against both hosts
- Attach the clean scan result to the PCI evidence pack

Notes:
- Restricted: scan results for card-data hosts are need-to-know until both hosts pass
- No sign of exploitation; the weakness is configuration only

comments.author: Ivan
comments.text: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are off on cde-web-01 and the local scan is clean. cde-web-02 goes in the Thursday maintenance window because it fronts the card vault.

comments.author: Zhao
comments.text: Thanks. Keep this restricted until both hosts pass the external scan, then attach the evidence and close it.

comments.author: Ivan
comments.text: Maintenance slot for cde-web-02 is booked for Thursday 22:00 SGT.
